construct: PAI-1, encoded by SERPINE1, inhibits tissue-type and urokinase-type plasminogen activators. Complete deficiency causes excessive conversion of plasminogen to plasmin and excessive fibrinolysis, producing delayed bleeding after trauma or surgery despite normal routine coagulation tests.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Delayed post-procedural bleeding with normal routine coagulation tests and biallelic SERPINE1 loss identifies complete PAI-1 deficiency. The direct hemostatic defect is loss of inhibition of tPA/uPA with excessive plasmin generation and fibrinolysis.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Factor XIII deficiency is the strongest clinical mimic because it can also cause delayed bleeding with normal PT/aPTT, but the proven SERPINE1 genotype fixes the mechanism as excessive fibrinolysis rather than defective fibrin cross-linking. The platelet/vWF options have different primary-hemostasis phenotypes.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Even an expert who recognizes factor XIII as a delayed-bleeding mimic cannot select it once SERPINE1 loss is given and the lead asks for the direct hemostatic abnormality.
